description:
Get your brand's SpiderGate usage — turns vs attempts, the outcome split, spend, and cost avoided.
These are the SAME numbers as the /dashboard/gate/usage page; the two must never disagree.

WINDOW: pass from/to (ISO-8601) for a real calendar range — "this month" is
from=2026-08-01T00:00:00Z&to=2026-09-01T00:00:00Z, which is NOT the same window as a rolling 30 days.
`days` is a DEPRECATED rolling lookback kept for one release and is ignored when from/to are given.

READ THE RESPONSE CAREFULLY:
- turn_metrics — a TURN is one logical request; ATTEMPTS include retries and provider fallbacks.
  Never quote a bare "requests": amplification = attempts / turns. If turns_complete is false,
  some attempts carry no trace_id and could not be folded into a turn.
- outcome — FOUR states, not three: delivered / hollow / failed / UNKNOWN. `unknown` is
  "we cannot tell" (rows predating the output_chars column), NOT a success. Folding it into
  delivered is a false all-clear. `measurable_from` says when the split became trustworthy;
  a window reaching before that date is partly unmeasurable.
- cost_avoided — a COUNTERFACTUAL against a reference list price (`reference_model`), not an invoice.
  `state` is "measured" or "unmeasurable"; never quote it as billing.

🔴 `by_provider` IS NOT THE PROVIDER. It carries the litellm WIRE PREFIX, so ~75,000 MiniMax rows
are stamped "openai". Never report it as the provider — an agent that does will attribute MiniMax
traffic to OpenAI and act on it. For the real provider use `gate_flow`, which resolves it through
the key's integration. Treat this field as a wire route, or ignore it.

Two more outcome details: `truncated` and `tool_call_turns` are ANNOTATIONS that overlap the four
states, not extra states — summing all six double-counts. And `window_predates_measurement: true`
means your window reaches back before the split could be measured at all, so `delivered_rate` is
computed over only the classifiable rows.

bucket.description: Grain of the `by_bucket` time series (default: day).

compare.description: Also return the immediately preceding window of identical length under `comparison`. Doubles the query cost.

days.description: DEPRECATED rolling lookback in days (1-366). Ignored when from/to are supplied — a lookback cannot express a calendar month.

from.description: Window start (inclusive), ISO-8601. Naive values read as UTC. Pair with `to` for a calendar range.

to.description: Window end (exclusive), ISO-8601. Defaults to now.

name: gate_usage
